title: a person confirmed on a primary record
line: the owner accepts one primary record and the rule follows: the gravesite locator's one card among namesakes is taken though the burial town differs from a bare claim, a second census takes the son on name, birth year and the claimed parent whose persona fits, the parents follow; a record attached on the owner's word with no step citing it is a fetch step done with a found run that a regeneration keeps and a re-read supersedes; a record's undated death asserts the file's one dated event, never a second; a rule decision's re-run is logged under the session that acted; a step nothing generates is dropped and named in the audit row; the rule judges a record by the collection its current reading gives, never the archive row's stale banner

steps.say: his Social Security record arrives: the file cites it, so it reaches his step; a card for him and for the parents it names

expect.why: a card for the record's subject, the person it was fetched for; the parents it names wait on him

rule.why: the name is not accepted yet

steps.say: the owner accepts him on it: his name and birth now rest on a trusted source

expect.why: the father the record names, in a stated relationship to the son just accepted and claimed by the file, is taken by the rule at once

steps.say: the gravesite locator's page for his name and death year: one card, his, among the namesakes

expect.why: the namesake who died the same year another day stays a hint
the card says the dates agree to the day and the burial town differs: the locator's postal town against the file's

has: disagrees with the tree's own claim, not yet accepted

expect.why: his name and dates on a trusted source, the card is taken: the burial town disagrees only with a bare claim, so it is named, not a veto

steps.say: the locator's first page of namesakes: ten decedents agreeing on the name alone make no card

expect.why: namesakes agreeing on the name alone are no hint

steps.say: the 1940 census of his parents' household: the rule takes him on name, birth year and the claimed parent whose persona fits, and the parents follow

expect.why: the confirmed son in the claimed parents' household is taken on his name, birth year and the stated parent
the father follows through the claimed route, the son's own persona fitting on more than a name
the mother, a name and the claimed spouse only, is one point short: a card for the owner

steps.say: a record attached on the owner's word, no step citing it: his father's death index page

expect.why: no step cited the record; a card on arrival for the record's subject, his
a fetch step written on his plan, done under the death record row, on the owner's word
the step's found run names the record

steps.say: his plan regenerated keeps the done step
the record read again: proposed again through the step, the first card superseded

expect.why: the first reading's card closed as superseded

steps.say: the owner accepts him on it: the record's undated death asserts the one Death event he already has, beside the file's dated claim

expect.why: he has one Death event already, the file's own claim; the record's own Death, with no date, asserts that same event rather than guessing a second one, and the key fact's basis is the accepted one

steps.say: that one statement rejected on its own: the key fact falls back to the file's claim

expect.why: the Ohio index's own statement on the shared event is rejected; the file's own statement stands on it as it always did, and is the value again

steps.say: a source with a window: a death in 2007 is within Legacy.com's, so his obituary row lists it first

expect.why: a death in 2007 is in Legacy.com's 1999-on window: its row lists H05 first

steps.say: a newspaper page from a connector's run, read with its manifest: a hit on the surname alone is no card and no hint

expect.why: a loc.gov page (public domain) is redistributable and its manifest names the registry row that said so
an Ancestry export is not
a newspaper hit on the surname alone makes no card and is no hint

steps.say: his remaining key facts decided on the file's claims: the baseline reviewed

expect.why: reviewed, the namesakes agreeing on the name alone are still no hint
reviewed, the surname-only newspaper hit is still no hint

steps.say: a rule decision's re-run of the matcher is logged as the session that acted

expect.why: the matcher's re-run after a rule decision is logged under the session that acted, not the owner alone

steps.say: a step nothing generates, written by hand
the plan regenerated drops it and names it in the run's audit row, the only trace of it afterwards

expect.why: the audit row names the dropped step by key, row and rationale

steps.say: a death record naming a woman as the deceased's mother, attached on the owner's word as hers: a card on the name alone

lacks: hint until a person reads it

steps.say: the same page archived once more under the banner title an older parser took for its collection

archive.collection: Mentioned in the Record of Ollie Duke Davidson (Lena Howard Bell's Son)

lacks: hint until a person reads it

expect.why: the rule judges the page by the collection its current reading gives (a death record, an identifying kind), never the archive row's banner title

steps.say: the step the owner's-word record fulfilled, reopened: the found rows stay, a reopen row is added under the run's source, and the record names nobody it was fetched for

expect.why: reopened, the record still names him, through the accepted link he keeps on it, not through the run
the found row stays as written; the reopen row carries the source of the run it reopens

steps.say: a found run at a source other than a planned fetch step's holder: the pages are held, the cited record is not

expect.why: a found run at a row-source connector is logged and the fetch step stays planned
the page's found run names him as a person it was fetched for

steps.say: that run reopened: the reopen row carries the run's source, not the step's own holder, and the record names him no more

reopen.note: harness: the other paper's page was not his after all

expect.why: the found row stays as it was; one reopen row added, under the source of the run it reopens
reopened, the record no longer names him

steps.say: the SSN record read again: the accepted links it already carries move to the new reading's personas, nothing waits on a card

expect.why: the son, the father and the mother were already decided on the first reading; carry_links moves all three, so the rule has nothing left to propose

steps.say: the old accepted link stays in person_persona as it was; the new reading carries its own

expect.why: one row on the superseded persona, one on the current: neither rewritten nor removed
read through the current reading alone, he is still the record's own subject: the extra row does not appear as a second, conflicting answer
the matcher's own reading of who is accepted on the record counts him once, through the current extraction, not once per reading

steps.say: the person screen's own view of the record: one extraction, his link on it accepted

expect.why: the superseded reading's own extraction and personas do not reach the screen at all
his persona on the current reading shows the accepted link the earlier reading's decision carried

steps.say: the plan settled and the catalog whole
